approved.title: Many models per instance — capture
approved.method: One process hosts N Pulse instances (N = 1, 10, 50, 100, 300, 500), each capturing batches of 50 rows of 20 features at 10 batches/s per model into one InfluxDB. Measure caller-side capture latency (p50/p99), rows/s written, queue depth, RSS, threads, open sockets, CPU.
approved.pass: capture p99 < 2 ms at every N; written = captured (0 loss) up to 300 models; RSS growth linear and < 30 MB/model
approved.expected_limit: one writer thread and one HTTP client per Pulse — thread and socket count may cap N

approved.title: High-volume sustained ingestion
approved.method: Ramp from 10k to 1M rows/min (single model and 100 models), 15 min per step. Measure ingestion lag, drops, InfluxDB CPU/RAM/disk, write latency, batch sizes; end-to-end reconciliation (rows queried back = rows captured).
approved.pass: zero loss below the saturation point; saturation point documented; drops counted exactly beyond it

approved.title: Storage outage under load, with and without spool
approved.method: At 200k rows/min, stop InfluxDB for 60 s, 10 min and 30 min; repeat with spool_dir and without. Measure capture latency during the outage, spooled/dropped rows, spool disk usage, replay duration, duplicates after replay.
approved.pass: with spool — 0 loss, 0 duplicates, capture p99 < 2 ms during the outage; without — drops counted exactly

approved.title: Process crash and restart
approved.method: kill -9 the capturing process mid-burst (spool on), restart, replay; count losses and duplicates.
approved.pass: losses limited to the in-memory queue at crash time, measured and documented; 0 duplicates

approved.title: Queue saturation and memory bound
approved.method: max_queue_rows from 1k to 1M under a burst 10x the write rate; measure RSS ceiling and drop accounting.
approved.pass: RSS stays under the bound implied by max_queue_rows; dropped_rows exact

approved.title: Schema evolution and type conflicts
approved.method: Mix optional fields, change a field type mid-stream, add/remove features; verify rejected_rows accounting and that valid rows are written.
approved.pass: every rejection counted with its reason; no retry loop; valid rows written

settings.scope: SC-01, SC-02, SC-03, SC-13 in both write profiles; SC-05 and SC-14 once (default)
settings.instructions: Rerun of the platform tests after pulsar_data_collection 0.10.0 / pulsar_metrics 0.11.0 (installed from main on every host). The modules lab/tests/sc_*.py exist and are final: do not rewrite them; fix only a crash, and say so. Same sizes as the night of 2026-11-02 so the numbers compare: SC-01 LAB_LEVELS=1,10,50,100,300,500 LAB_STEP_S=60; SC-02 LAB_STEP_S=180 (default rates and model sets); SC-03 LAB_OUTAGES=60,600,1800 with the black hole; SC-13 LAB_REPS=3. SC-05 and SC-14 use no shared writer: run them once with LAB_PROFILE=default LAB_RUN_TAG=default. InfluxDB 2.6.1 on lab-db with ulimit nofile 65536 and LAB_INFLUX_CONTAINER set so SC-01 measures server descriptors. Run the tests one after the other (they share InfluxDB). Never lab-soak, lab-cpu or GPU hosts.
settings.report_instructions: This is the scalability rerun, not a night lab: write the report in French as a comparison. For each test and metric, give the night's value (lab/results/<id>.json, profile before the fixes), the default profile and the tuned profile (lab/results/<id>.<profile>.json), and say for each limit M31-M38, m18-m24 of the night report (settings.night_report) whether it is fixed, improved or still present, with the numbers.
